articles.title: Rams’ travel plan was a bust, never to be repeated
articles.summary: It turns out that traveling to Australia a day before the game might’ve been a bad idea
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams ' travel plan for their game against the 49ers in Australia on Thursday proved a massive bust. LA's plan was risky from the start and should never be repeated by a team traveling to the continent again.

Both the Rams and 49ers had different strategies for going down under (hate how that was phrased, but I guess I'll allow it). San Francisco got there a week before the game, while Los Angeles arrived in Melbourne just over a day before kickoff. The Rams apparently thought they had figured out jet lag, consulting experts beforehand to figure out what to do.

Regardless of the thought put into their plan, it failed mightily, with a humbling and embarrassing 27-7 final on the scoreboard once the clocks hit triple zeroes.

While no NFL team had ever traveled to Australia before this season, the Rams weren't strangers to the international scene. They should have known better, even if the destination was uncharted territory for the league.

In their previous three overseas games, the team was 3-0, including a win over the Jaguars in London last October, where they deployed a similar travel plan. That worked to perfection as they blew out the eventual AFC South champs by 28 points.

However, the Rams had an easier time on that trip in particular because they flew directly from Baltimore to London, since they played the Ravens the week before, according to ESPN . By doing that, LA cut an 11-hour flight to seven hours.

For those of you who don't know geography well — clearly the Rams' coaching staff didn't — Melbourne, Australia is quite a trek from the West Coast. The flight was over double what the team flew from Baltimore to London. To illustrate how baffling the plan was from the get-go, new 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans had a priceless reaction upon learning when LA arrived.

Putting a travel plan together is one thing, and executing it is another. Even with all the backing and research beforehand, all that added stress on the body from the extra-long flight clearly caught up with them. The Rams appeared sluggish throughout the game, and even an apparent super team couldn't overcome the added challenges.

When I flew to Hawaii from Chicago a few years ago, I felt incredibly off from the moment I stepped off the plane. So, I cannot imagine traveling as far as the Rams did and playing a football game in such a short window.

During his postgame press conference, Sean McVay said the plan wasn't the reason why the team "didn't play well enough," even if it were easy to pin the blame.

Hopefully the Rams learned something valuable about international travel following this debacle. One bone-headed travel plan shouldn't define the rest of the season. Being outclassed by a bitter rival right out of the gate is about the worst possible way to start a season, but LA still has a great team that should be fine once it returns to play on American soil.

The Rams served as guinea pigs for their travel plan to Australia in the opener and were on the wrong side of things. Unfortunately, LA is now the poster child for what not to do whenever the league plays in Australia next.

articles.title: County Championship: Ben Stokes back in top flight as Durham promoted after victory over Middlesex
articles.summary: Durham complete return to domestic cricket's top flight by beating Middlesex with Callum Parkinson and Brydon Carse claiming four wickets apiece; Olly Stone took five as Nottinghamshire beat Hampshire and JT Langridge did likewise as Gloucestershire beat Lancashire
articles.body:
The north-east side began the final day needing eight wickets and Kasey Aldridge struck with the first ball to set the tone.

Despite a battling unbeaten ton from Harry Duke alongside Ben Geddes' half-century, Durham took control with the ball as Callum Parkinson finished with four wickets for 45 runs and Brydon Carse also claimed four to secure their spot back in the top flight next year.

Elsewhere in Division Two, Gloucestershire secured a 105-run win over Lancashire , with JT Langridge putting in an impressive performance with the ball.

The bowler struck early to remove both George Balderson and Noman Ali before Sai Kishore claimed Mitchell Stanley's wicket.

Langridge secured victory for Gloucestershire and completed a five-wicket haul by dismissing Rocky Flintoff for 65.

Hampshire remain under pressure in Division One following a 54-run defeat to Nottinghamshire .

Olly Stone earned a five-for by taking six wickets for 28 runs to keep Nottinghamshire in the race for the title, but Hampshire remain at the foot of the standings, 32 points adrift of safety, with two more games to go.
